newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-VAN DER WESTHUIZEN BREAKS WELSH HEARTS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-VAN DER WESTHUIZEN BREAKS WELSH HEARTS.

text.p: South African coach Andre Markgraaff was a contented man after watching his side end an exhausting year on Sunday with their sixth successive test win.

The Springboks ran in five tries in a 37-20 win over Wales and could have had 10 as their pack controlled a hard forward battle and scrum-half Joost van der Westhuizen snapped up a personal hat-trick.

It means South Africa have now completed their mission on tour of Argentina, France and Wales by winning all their five tests. For good measure they also beat the All Blacks at Ellis Park in the last test of this year's home series.
"South Africa won the World Cup last year because of their defence," said Markgraaff, villified at home after omitting skipper Francois Pienaar from the tour squad.

"We are trying to score tries now and given we have now scored about 20 in five tests it means we are improving in certain areas. We have built a good side with a good team spirit and I am looking forward to 1997."
The 25-year-old Van der Westhuizen, who now has 12 tries in 26 tests, was at the heart of his team's impressive performance.
He scored his first try in the 10th minute following a 60-metre charge from Ruben Kruger and midway through the first-half the Springboks struck again.

Sustained driving from the forwards set up Kruger who put skipper Gary Teichmann and Henry Honiball away down the left. Honiball's pass to Andre Joubert was close to being forward, but referee Sateve Lander awarded the try.

Just before the break Van der Westhuizen scored his second when he sliced through the defence and the Springboks killed the game at the start of the second-half when the same player burrowed his way over from close range to complete his hat-trick.

The Springboks, who added another try from Jaques Olivier in the 54th minute, then sat back and allowed the Welsh to start taking the game to them, inspired by some excellent work by their midfield pair of Scott Gibbs and Allan Bateman.
The home side had kept in touch with five penalties from full-back Neil Jenkins and, in the last minute, Arwel Thomas slipped through from close range to provide a consolation try.
"Wales played like they wanted to make it a great test match and for that they must be congratulated," said Markgraaff.
Welsh captain Jonathan Humphreys was full of praise for the Springboks. "They're not far off the best side in the world," he said. "There's not much between them and New Zealand."

Wales - 15-Neil Jenkins; 14-Ieuan Evans, 13-Scott Gibbs, 12-Allen Bateman, 11-Dafydd James; 10-Jonathan Davies, 9-Rob Howley; 8-Steve Williams, 7-Colin Charvis, 6-Dale McIntosh (19-Nathan Thomas, 67th), 5-Mark Rowley, 4-Gareth Llewellyn, 3-David Young, 2-Jonathan Humphreys (captain), 1-Christian Loader.

South Africa - 15-Andre Joubert; 14-James Small, 13-Japie Mulder, 12-Hennie le Roux, 11-Jacques Olivier (16-Andre Snyman, 75th); 10-Henry Honiball, 9-Joost van der Westhuizen; 8-Gary Teichmann (captain), 7-Andre Venter, 6-Ruben Kruger, 5-Mark Andrews(22-Hannes Strydom, 42nd), 4-Kobus Wiese, 3-Adrian Garvey, 2-James Dalton, 1-Dawie Theron (24-Toks van der Linde, 20th)
